topics.label: Introduction to the complement lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture by emphasizing complement's importance and acknowledging its difficult terminology.

topics.label: Overview of complement activation and functions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces complement as an inactive blood-protein system whose activation supports immune defence and clearance.

topics.label: Complement nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the naming conventions and historical exceptions needed to follow the complement cascade.

topics.label: C3 activation and the three complement pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how C3 becomes activated and accumulates on pathogen surfaces until complement reaches its activation threshold.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of activated complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how activated complement produces the immune responses that eliminate pathogens.

topics.label: Complement regulation and host-cell protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how regulatory proteins restrain complement activation to prevent damage to host cells.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic connects deficiencies in particular complement components or regulators to their distinct clinical presentations.

topics.label: Staphylococcus aureus complement evasion and protein A applications
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how bacterial adaptations evade complement and how protein A's evasion mechanism can be exploited clinically and experimentally.

topics.label: Lecture close and transition to adaptive immunity
topics.groupedBecause: This closing ends the complement lecture and identifies adaptive immunity as the subject of the next lecture.
